title: The soul at peace
hookLine: O soul at peace, return: said at death, or on the Day of Judgment?
tomorrow: what would it be like to see the One you've prayed to?

lines: BUT AH! THOU SOUL AT PEACE!
cards: Some voice notes get replayed just for the tone: someone you love saying your name like they're glad you exist.

The Qur'an has a call like that near the end of the surah called the Dawn, in Pickthall's words: "But ah! thou soul at peace! Return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure! Enter thou among My bondmen! Enter thou My Garden!"
So who is being called, and when? Muslim commentators have answered that in more than one way.

teach.b: The soul at peace is al-nafs al-mutma'innah: the self that has settled, that rests in Allah instead of running. Not a soul that never struggled; a soul that came to rest. Now the debate about the moment.

One view: these words are said at death. Some early commentators reported that the angels speak them to the believer's soul as it leaves. At its best, this view puts a gentle welcome at the hardest door.

teach.h: VIEW TWO: SAID ON THAT DAY.
teach.b: The other view: they're said on the Day of Judgment.
The verses just before describe that Day, the earth ground down and the angels in ranks, so the call comes as the answer to all of it: enter among My servants, enter My Garden.
At its best, this view keeps the verses in their place in the surah. Some commentators, such as Ibn Kathir, mention both. And both views share the heart of it.
The Arabic pairs two words: radiyah, pleased, and mardiyyah, pleasing.
The soul is pleased with its Lord, and its Lord is pleased with it. One small detail: in these verses, the soul isn't sent anywhere. It's invited back.

how: Muslims recite Surah al-Fajr's closing verses (89:27–30) in prayer and sometimes at funerals and graves; commentators differ on whether the call comes at death or on the Day of Judgment, and some hold both.

games.q: what does “the soul at peace” mean?
o: a self settled in Allah, called back to Him
a soul resting in the grave until it's judged
a person whose life has had no troubles in it

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: the soul at peace, settled in Allah
said to the soul at death
said on the Day of Judgment

s: the soul at peace is someone who never struggled
it's a soul that came to rest in Allah, not one that never had to.
Muslim commentators all agree on exactly when 89:27 is spoken
some say at death, some on the Day of Judgment; some, like Ibn Kathir, mention both.
in the verses, the soul is both pleased and pleasing
radiyah, mardiyyah: pleased with its Lord, and its Lord pleased with it.

games.q: your dad says 89:27 is spoken on the Day of Judgment. your grandmother says it's said at death, and you agree with her. what's your dad's best case?
o: the verses come right after the passage about that Day, as its answer.
death is too sad a moment for words this hopeful.
Allah speaks to souls only on the Day of Judgment.
games.why: at its best, the Judgment-Day reading keeps the call in its place in the surah: the answer to the Day just described. the at-death reading's best case: a welcome at the hardest door.

practice: Find the quietest sound around you: a fan, a fridge's hum, your own breath. Rest your attention on it, the way a settled soul rests instead of running. When your mind runs off, come back to the sound.

wordCard.voice: The soul at peace: the self that has settled in Allah, called home in the Qur'an, pleased with its Lord and pleasing to Him.

orig.note: Arabic: the soul at peace, the self at rest (Qur'an 89:27).

carryVoice: The call to carry: return, pleased, and welcomed home as pleasing to Him. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: But ah! thou soul at peace! Return unto thy Lord, content in His good pleasure! Enter thou among My bondmen! Enter thou My Garden!

sources.ref: Qur'an 89:21–26: the Day when the earth is ground to powder and the Lord comes with the angels, rank on rank
Ibn Kathir, Tafsir on 89:27–30: reports that the words are said at death, and that they are said on the Day of Resurrection
